blocks.text: New, used, manufactured or modular homes for sale in South Surrey

parts.t: The mobile homes for sale in South Surrey on this page are resale homes listed on the MLS®. Most are manufactured homes in a park on a rented pad, single-wide or double-wide. A resale home can be a few years old or several decades old, so its age, its CSA label and the park's rules matter as much as the asking price.

Manufactured home and mobile home mean the same thing: a home built in a factory, moved to its site in one or two sections and registered in BC's Manufactured Home Registry. A modular home is also built in a factory, but to the A-277 standard, and it is set on a permanent foundation on land you own, so it is usually bought and financed like a house.

A brand-new manufactured or modular home is normally ordered through a manufacturer's dealer, or bought as a new unit that a park has already placed on a pad. I am a REALTOR®, not a dealer. I help you buy a resale home on the MLS® in South Surrey, or a new home that a park or builder has listed, and I check the label, the registry record, the pad rent and the park's approval rules before you remove subjects.

blocks.text: Known 55+ manufactured-home parks and co-ops: what the sources show

These are the 55+ places named in public sources where you can own the home. Pad rent, shares and fees quoted below come from one listing on one date, not a park's posted rates, so confirm them with the park.
Sea Ridge Bays — 15875 20 Ave (King George Corridor, South Surrey)

Sea Ridge Bays is the only 55+ manufactured-home community in South Surrey. Listings say it is 55+ and a bare-land strata with "low monthly fees: $210 includes water", with a clubhouse, plenty of visitor parking and up to two dogs of any size. Another listing mentions council approval for buyers. There's no pad rent: you own your lot as a strata lot and pay a strata fee, so strata law applies, not the park tenancy rules.
Rules that affect 55+ park homes

items.t: Manufactured-home parks are governed by tenancy law, not strata law: the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and its regulation apply, and the strata age-bylaw rules don't. A seller must give the buyer the written tenancy agreement and park rules, and selling means assigning the pad tenancy, which needs the park owner's consent.

A park's 55+ rule has its own legal basis: BC's manufactured home park rules recognize parks where every pad is reserved for someone 55 or older (or two or more people, at least one of them 55 or older), and the park owner can refuse a sale where no buyer meets that age. That's how the 55+ rules at the three Newton and Fleetwood parks work; I don't know of any pad-rental park in South Surrey.

Consent has a deadline: a seller can assign the pad tenancy only with the landlord's written consent first (or deemed consent), an arbitrator's order, or where the tenancy agreement allows it. The park owner must answer within 10 days of the written request (RTB Form 10), silence counts as consent, and no fee can be charged. Before asking, the seller must give the buyer written copies of the park rules and the relevant parts of the tenancy agreement.

Pad rent increases are capped: A park landlord may increase rent only with 3 full months' notice, only once every 12 months, and only up to the yearly limit — 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027; the proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of manufactured home sites in the park; further increases require a Residential Tenancy Branch application. On assignment, the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same, as does the scheduled date of a subsequent rent increase.

Park closure or conversion: if a landlord plans to convert all or much of a park to another use, they must have all the government permits and approvals first, give 12 months' notice, and pay each tenant $20,000 by the date the notice takes effect. The tenant can move out early with at least 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can apply for more compensation (the home's assessed value minus the $20,000). Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw (2025) doesn't apply to manufactured home parks.

Registration is what makes a sale effective, and the CSA label is a sale gate: In BC, the sale, transfer or purchase of a manufactured home is only effective if registered with the Manufactured Home Registry, through a lawyer or notary filing the Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership forms. A home may not be sold unless it has the original legible CSA decal attached (Z-240 for mobile homes, A-277 for modular); if the label is lost, Technical Safety BC has a licensed electrical contractor inspect the wiring, and the electrical approval label prepared can be used in place of a CSA label. A permit to move a home is issued by the Registry and expires 30 days after issue.

Taxes on a home in a park: the Province states a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value will not include the value of the land if the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.

By contrast, strata rules apply at Sea Ridge Bays. In BC, the only legal strata age bylaw is 55 and older, and it limits who can live in a home, not who can own it. Exemptions cover existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, a younger spouse or partner, children under 19 in the resident's care, and adult children the resident cared for before they turned 19. Strata rental restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022.
Zoning: check a specific park's zone on the City's COSMOS map.

OCP: Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2026, No. 21900: is the current OCP — adopted June 15, 2026, replacing Bylaw No. 18020. White Rock addresses, if any appear, fall under White Rock's own OCP Bylaw 2017, No. 2220 instead.

blocks.text: Good to know before you buy a park home

items.t: South Surrey's only 55+ manufactured-home community is not a park at all, and the clue is in its listings. Sea Ridge Bays' listings say "Council Approval Required" and record title as Freehold Strata — its buyers get strata documents and a Form B, not a tenancy agreement and park rules, and its 55+ rule is a strata bylaw with provincial exemptions a park does not offer.
The tenure, not the structure, drives the price shape inside one feed. Individual card prices are feed data that change and are not frozen here as facts.

Two Surrey parks share almost the same name, in two different communities — and neither is in South Surrey. Westwood Court is the Fleetwood park at 8670 156 Street; Westwood Estates is the Newton park on 134 Street, whose own listings disagree on 8224 vs 8254 as the civic address. A South Surrey buyer searching "Westwood" is looking at Newton / Fleetwood product.

Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw (2025) doesn't cover any park on this page, because it doesn't apply to manufactured home parks. Park residents' protection if a park is redeveloped comes from the provincial rules: permits first, 12 months' notice and $20,000 compensation.

blocks.text: South Surrey: streets and boundaries

items.t: South Surrey's manufactured-home communities all sit in the King George Corridor, in the blocks around King George Boulevard, 160 Street, 20 Avenue, and Cranley Drive, between 8 Avenue and the Nicomekl River with Highway 99 on the east side.

The corridor's flood setting is defined by two rivers: the Serpentine and Nicomekl River Sea Dams limit ocean tides from backwatering up the two rivers and protect about 51 square kilometres of lowland, including Highways 10, 15, and 99.

Surrey's manufactured-home zoning for the corridor is the Manufactured Home Residential Zone (RM-M) under Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, Part 19, which is the zone the City applies to manufactured home parks.

blocks.text: Mobile homes in South Surrey: what you will find

items.t: Breakaway Bays, 1840 160 Street, is a pad-rental community where the buyer owns the home and rents the pad; the operator Parkbridge's own page lists the property address as 1840 160th Street, Surrey, British Columbia V4A 4X4, calls it a Residential Retirement Community, and lists an outdoor heated pool open May to September.

Sea Ridge Bays, 15875 20 Avenue, is a bare-land strata: the buyer owns the home and the strata lot, pays a strata fee, and pays no pad rent. A City of Surrey planning report confirms 15875-20 Avenue is one large lot on the north side of 20 Avenue between King George Boulevard and Highway 99, with underlying RM-M zoning and Land Use Contract No. 283 dating from 1977.

blocks.text: Rules for buying mobile homes in South Surrey

items.t: Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw No. 21788 (2025) does not apply to property governed by the MHPTA, so park residents rely on Policy O-34A and the provincial act instead of the bylaw that covers ordinary rental buildings.

The RM-M zone sets the physical form of a park: a minimum manufactured home space of 225 square metres (2,420 square feet) with a minimum width of 12 metres, a maximum density of 22 dwelling units per hectare, and permitted uses limited to a manufactured home park plus one single-family dwelling for the park manager.

blocks.text: South Surrey: details most buyers miss

items.t: Surrey publishes a plain-language manufactured home park policy brochure that walks through pad rent, the 12-month notice rule, and the compensation rule, which most buyers never see before they start shopping.

Policy O-34A dates from a July 27, 2015 revision recorded in Corporate Report R167, so Surrey's park redevelopment process is a council policy, not a bylaw, and it can be changed by Council resolution.

When the City reported on Sea Ridge Bays, the property still had a 1977 land use contract (No. 283) on top of its manufactured home zoning. Have a lawyer explain how the old contract and the current zoning work together.

Replacement of the Nicomekl Sea Dam, one of the two dams holding back tidal flooding near the corridor, is on hold pending direction from the Province, according to a City corporate report dated November 3, 2025.
The two Surrey sea dams are more than 100 years old and protect about 51 square kilometres that include the Highway 99 corridor east of the parks.

items.t: For 2026, Surrey's annual flat utility rates for a single-family dwelling are 1,195 dollars for water and 1,661 dollars for sewer, a combined 2,856 dollars, while metered accounts are billed every four months.

blocks.text: South Surrey: getting around

items.t: TransLink runs transit in South Surrey, and its Surrey–Delta system map shows route 321 on King George Boulevard and route 345 on 152 Street serving the corridor south toward White Rock Centre.
Highway 99 forms the east edge of the King George Corridor, so the parks sit between the King George Boulevard bus corridor and the freeway.

blocks.text: Buying mobile homes in South Surrey: risks to check

items.t: Flood due diligence here is about the river system, not just the lot: the Serpentine and Nicomekl sea dams hold back tidal water for about 51 square kilometres of lowland, and the Nicomekl dam's replacement is paused awaiting provincial direction, so a buyer should ask how the specific community is protected.

Tenure confusion is the local trap: two communities a few blocks apart run on opposite rules — pad tenancy at Breakaway Bays, bare-land strata at Sea Ridge Bays — so the form of ownership must be confirmed from title and strata or park documents, not from how a home is marketed.

At a strata community, the buyer should read the strata plan and bylaws; at a pad-rental park, the park rules form part of the tenancy agreement, and the RTB Form 10 consent step must be built into the purchase timeline.

faq.q: Are there new mobile homes for sale in South Surrey?
faq.a: Sometimes. A park occasionally places a new manufactured home on a vacant pad and lists it on the MLS®, and it shows in the listings on this page while it is available. Most South Surrey listings are resale homes. To order a home from a factory, you deal with a manufactured-home dealer.

faq.q: What is the difference between a manufactured, mobile and modular home?
faq.a: Manufactured and mobile mean the same home: factory-built, moved in one or two sections and registered in BC's Manufactured Home Registry. A modular home is factory-built to the A-277 standard and set on a permanent foundation on land you own, so it is usually bought and financed like a house.

faq.q: Is Jared Gibbons a mobile home dealer?
faq.a: No. Jared is a REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty. He represents buyers and sellers of manufactured homes listed on the MLS® in South Surrey and across the Fraser Valley. He does not sell new units from a lot.

faq.q: Which South Surrey manufactured-home communities are actually 55+?
faq.a: One verifies: Sea Ridge Bays (15875 20 Ave), a bare-land strata where you own the lot — listings state "Sea Ridge Bays is 55+" and record title as Freehold Strata. No pad-rent park in South Surrey verifies as 55+; Surrey's three 55+ parks are in Fleetwood and Newton. The Cranley Drive community's 55+ claim comes only from listings.

faq.q: What do I own when I buy in a park, versus at Sea Ridge Bays?
faq.a: In a park, only the manufactured home: you rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, and buying means taking over that tenancy, which needs the park owner's written consent first and registration with the Manufactured Home Registry. At Sea Ridge Bays you own the strata lot too, pay a strata fee instead of pad rent, and review strata documents.

faq.q: Can a park raise my pad rent when I buy, or charge me for approving me?
faq.a: No to both mechanics: on assignment the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same and the scheduled date of a subsequent increase does not change; increases otherwise need 3 full months' notice, at most once every 12 months, capped at the yearly limit (2.3% plus the proportional amount for 2026). Consent itself cannot be charged for, and the park owner must respond within 10 days of a written request — silence counts as consent.

faq.q: Can I rely on the parks, operator and 50+ covenant named for Cranley Drive?
faq.a: Not yet. Pull the park rules, the tenancy agreement and the title documents for the specific home before writing.

faq.q: What are the carrying costs on top of the purchase?
faq.a: Ownership type decides the monthly cost: a park home pays pad rent, while Sea Ridge Bays pays a strata fee instead (listings say $210 a month including water). Confirm the current amount for a specific home in the tenancy agreement or the Form B.

Community by community: Sea Ridge Bays listings state two dogs with no size restrictions; Westwood Court listings state pets welcome; Westwood Estates allows large dogs with park approval, no vicious breeds; Newton Mobile Home Park listings state one pet, subject to park rules.

faq.q: What if the home has lost its CSA label?
faq.a: A manufactured home may not be sold unless it has the original and legible CSA decal attached (Z-240 for a mobile home, A-277 for a modular). If the label is removed or lost, the home must be re-certified: Technical Safety BC arranges a licensed electrical contractor's inspection, and the electrical approval label prepared can be used in place of a CSA label to list the home for sale.

faq.q: What happens if a park is redeveloped?
faq.a: The rules are set out: the landlord must have all permits and approvals first, then give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 compensation by the date the notice takes effect, with more owed in some cases. Surrey's 2025 Tenant Protection Bylaw doesn't cover park residents.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ pad-rental park in South Surrey?
faq.a: None that I know of. Sea Ridge Bays — a bare-land strata, not a pad park — is the one 55+ manufactured-home community here.

faq.q: Does the park have to approve me, and can it charge for that?
faq.a: Yes to approval, no to a fee: assignment needs the park owner's prior written consent on RTB Form 10, with a response due by the 10th day and silence deemed consent; no fee may be charged for consent. Build the 10-day window into subject dates.

faq.q: What is the real difference between Breakaway Bays and Sea Ridge Bays?
faq.a: The difference is what you own. At Breakaway Bays, 1840 160 Street, you own the manufactured home only and rent the pad under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. At Sea Ridge Bays, 15875 20 Avenue, you own the home and the bare-land strata lot under it, so there is no pad rent and a strata fee applies instead, and strata rules replace park tenancy rules.

faq.q: If a South Surrey park is redeveloped, what notice and compensation do I get?
faq.a: The park owner may only require you to leave after every permit and approval is in place. The City's policy brochure states the owner must then give 12 months' notice and pay 20,000 dollars in compensation on or before the notice date, and a tenant who finds somewhere else sooner may end the tenancy early with 10 days' written notice.

faq.q: How much can pad rent rise at a rented-pad park here?
faq.a: Only by the provincial percentage, the same as everywhere in British Columbia.

faq.q: Does Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw protect me in a manufactured home park?
faq.a: No, and that surprises many buyers. The City states that Tenant Protection Bylaw No. 21788 does not apply to property governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, so a park household's protection on redevelopment comes from the provincial act and from City Policy O-34A, including its occupant prenotification steps, rather than from the bylaw.

faq.q: How much can pad rent go up?
faq.a: Up to the yearly limit — 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — once every 12 months, on 3 full months' notice. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of sites in the park; on assignment to a new owner the rent and the next increase date carry over unchanged.

faq.q: What happens if a South Surrey park closes or is converted?
faq.a: If a park is redeveloped, section 42 of the Act sets the steps: the landlord must first have all permits and approvals, then give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 compensation on or before the effective date. Tenants can leave early with 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can claim more, up to the home's assessed value minus the $20,000. If the landlord doesn't go ahead within a reasonable time, they owe a further payment of $5,000 or 12 months' rent, whichever is greater.
